analysis.title: USA: Payroll Growth Well Above Expectations and Revised Higher for Prior Months; Unemployment Rate Falls to 4.1%
key_insights: Nonfarm payrolls rose 165k in October vs GS +75k and median forecast +70k. Private payrolls rose 159k vs GS +70k and median +65k.
September payrolls were revised up 31k to 60k and August up 53k to 186k. The three-month average is 137k vs 51k before the report.
GS's estimate of underlying job growth, based on the payroll and household surveys, is 124k vs 51k before the report.
The payrolls diffusion index rose 1.8pt to 60.4 on a three-month basis, its highest since June 2023.
Healthcare added 55k, in line with the past three years' trend. Professional and business services added 70k and was revised up by 52k across August and September.

GS has argued many professional services occupations face higher AI displacement risk, but notes activity there is running closer to capacity, perhaps because firms are helping other companies manage the AI transition.

Durable goods manufacturing added 25k, likely supported by AI-related capex, data center construction, fiscal incentives for manufacturing investment and fading tariff uncertainty. Transportation and warehousing also added 25k.
The report fits the historical pattern of stronger October payrolls after a weak September when Labor Day falls late in the month, as it did this year.
The unemployment rate fell 0.03pp to 4.14% (reported 4.1%), vs GS and median forecast 4.2%. Employment rose 463k and the labor force rose 421k.

Labor force participation rose 0.1pp to 61.9% and is 0.2pp below the January level when benchmark revisions took effect. The 25-34 group rose 0.2pp, likely partly because of the June sampling bias rotating out of the household survey.

Household employment, adjusted for survey differences and BLS population estimate changes, rose 848k. U6 underemployment rose 0.3pp to 7.9% after September's lowest level since December 2024, mostly from +171k marginally attached workers.
Average hourly earnings rose 0.37% m/m vs GS and median +0.3%. The y/y rate fell 0.04pp to 3.12%. Production and non-supervisory wages rose 0.37% m/m and 3.31% y/y.
GS's wage tracker is 3.0% annualized and 3.4% y/y in Q3, and its wage survey leading indicator is 3.4% in October.
